summary: A small brick tower with corner turrets on the walls of El Morro fort at San Juan harbor, built 1908 on the base of a Spanish-era light first lit in the 1840s or 1853.

access.note: On the grounds of San Juan National Historic Site (fort open daily 9 am-5 pm per NPS); tower listed as closed by LighthouseFriends; check with the park.

notes_for_editor: Thin-to-moderate evidence: no keeper detail beyond the USLHS roster (NARA registers via Kraig Anderson) and one Bulletin obituary (Domingo Suarez Rosa, Port San Juan among six stations, no dates; not linked to the roster). Lighthouse Board reports for 1902-1920 are not in the corpus, so the 1908 rebuild is sourced only to LighthouseFriends and the NRHP form. Disagreements stated in the text: first light (1846 vs 1853, and 1 Jan vs August 1846), the 1899 tower (concrete per NRHP/LF, iron per the 1901 report, brick per National Park Planner; builder Navy vs insular government), lens date (1908 vs 1875 vs 1880), height (171 ft in 1901, 180.75 ft USLHS). The NRHP text is OCR; its Spanish-era dates should be glanced at. National Park Planner is a private visitor site; LighthouseFriends was used for facts only and in my own words. Wikipedia was used for leads only and is not cited. Visiting: LighthouseFriends says tower closed; NPS hours 9-5 vs LighthouseFriends 9-6; Wikipedia claims tower tours, unverified. Record's tower 'built 1846, 15.5 m, standing' conflates the 1846 first tower with the 1908 tower (the 1846 tower no longer stands).
